message.content:
**United States – Gini Coefficient (most recent estimate)**  

| Year | Gini Coefficient | Source |
|------|------------------|--------|
| 2019 | **0.485** (48.5 %) | U.S. Census Bureau, *Income Inequality* (Table 3.1) |
| 2022 | **0.485** (48.5 %) | World Bank, *Gini Index* (latest available data) |

> **Interpretation**  
> The Gini coefficient ranges from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (perfect inequality). A value of 0.485 indicates that income distribution in the United States is moderately unequal, with roughly half of the inequality concentrated among the top 20 % of earners.

> **Methodology & Notes**  
> * The U.S. Census Bureau calculates the Gini coefficient using household income data from the Current Population Survey (CPS).  
> * The World Bank’s figure is derived from national accounts and household surveys, and it is updated annually.  
> * Both sources report similar values, suggesting stability in the U.S. income inequality trend over the past decade.

> **Further Reading**  
> * U.S. Census Bureau – Income Inequality: <https://www.census.gov/data/tables/2019/demo/income-poverty/income-inequality.html>  
> * World Bank – Gini Index (World Development Indicators): <https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/SI.POV.GINI>  

If you need a more granular breakdown (e.g., by state or by decade), let me know!
